To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
photochemical, biological and chemical transformations of dissolved organic matter in atmospherically acid-ified lakes can produce alkalinity and thus reduce the acidity of the lakes.

the photochemical, chemical, biological, and hydrolytic transformations of dissolved organic matter are significant mechanisms of alkalinity production in lakes and that the importance of these processes is related to the DOC and A 1 loading.
photochemical degradation of DOC is a major source of biologically available organic C and of inorganic Al, and that it can significantly affect the alkalinity budget of a lake.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the photochemical degradation of DOC can lead to the formation of biologically available organic acids that can be further metabolized by bacteria.
